title: WHAT WOULD SELLING THIS SERVICE LOOK LIKE?
content:
Once you have a service idea, the next question is what the customer would actually buy.

A skill is not yet an offer. "I do bookkeeping" tells someone your field. An offer begins to define who you help, what work you perform, what is included, how the engagement works, and what outcome or useful result the customer is seeking.

ONE-OFF OR RECURRING
Some services naturally happen once, such as a home organization project or a logo design. Others naturally repeat, such as monthly bookkeeping, weekly cleaning, or ongoing maintenance. Some can be sold either way.

CUSTOM OR PRODUCTIZED
A custom service changes substantially for each client. A productized service has a more standardized scope, process, and deliverable. Standardization can make the service easier to explain and deliver, but it only works when customers actually need a sufficiently similar result.

LOCAL OR REMOTE
Some work requires physical presence. Other services can be delivered remotely. This affects your customer pool, travel, scheduling, tools, and operating costs.

YOUR TIME MATTERS
Estimate how much direct work one customer requires. Then ask how many customers you could serve without creating a schedule you do not want.

NEXT STEP
PDF 43 uses ChatGPT to turn the service idea into a specific direction.

A CONCRETE EXAMPLE

"I can do bookkeeping" can become several different businesses. One version could provide a one-time cleanup of messy books before tax preparation. Another could provide recurring monthly bookkeeping for small home-service businesses. Another could specialize in accounts payable and receivable support.

The skill overlaps, but what the customer buys is different.

Do not worry about creating a perfect package yet. First decide what kind of engagement makes sense for the customer and for your available capacity.

WHERE TO GO NEXT
Continue to PDF 43 to explore the service idea with ChatGPT.
